To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a new middle-class culture in Durban, but it is not a single, unified culture.
there are three main factors that are driving consumption: the need to maintain status and to display it, the need for self-expression, and the need to be part of a community.

the new black middle-class in Durban has a distinctive lifestyle, but it is not as yet an emergent national class culture; it is a lifestyle that has much in common with that of the white middle class, but it is also a lifestyle that is very different from that of the white class; and it is also very different from the lifestyle of the working class, but it has a lot of things in common with that class.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which consumption is a key site for the negotiation of social identities in South Africa.
the ways in which consumption practices are being used by South African people to negotiate their identities and their relationships in the context of the new South Africa.
how the new middle class is being constituted in Durban, and what this means for South African society as a whole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
South African consumption patterns and the new middle class are still in a state of becoming.
the new black middle-class in Durban is not yet a coherent social group.
South Africans have a lot in common, but also a lot to argue about.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are many new forms of consumption, many new forms of community and many new forms of sociality, but there are no new forms of society.
the middle classes are still in the making.
there is an emergence of a new middle class, but one that is highly diverse in terms of its cultural, racial and economic composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumption is not a neutral or innocent activity, and that it is not simply a question of the ability to purchase goods and services.
the black middle class is a very heterogeneous group, and that the ‘black diamond’ is not the only type of middle class person to be encountered in the new South Africa.
there is no single middle class in South Africa, and the term should be used only in a comparative sense.
